extraction.name: AMASS
extraction.description: A large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization.
extraction.creator: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael J. Black
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset is an amalgamation of 15 mocap datasets. Publicly available datasets were downloaded from the internet, while others were obtained privately or recorded by the authors using an optical motion capture system synchronized with a 4D scanning system.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Problems with the mocap data, such as swapped or mislabeled markers, were manually inspected and either corrected or excluded.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of sparse optical marker-based motion capture (mocap) data from 15 different datasets, with varying numbers of markers placed at different locations on the body, as well as high-resolution 4D body scans.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset collects physical human attributes, specifically identity-dependent body shape parameters, poses, and soft-tissue dynamics from human subjects.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep learning and computer vision applications.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly hosted at a dedicated URL, and the maintainers plan to continuously expand it and support the community in adding new shared captures.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Raw motion capture data with varying marker sets from 15 different datasets were converted and unified into a single standardized format (SMPL body models) using the MoSh++ method.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: The publicly available datasets were downloaded from the internet. We obtained several other datasets privately or recorded them ourselves (Dancers, Transitions, BioMotionLab and SSM)... To record this dataset we use an optical motion capture system synchronized and calibrated together with a high resolution 4D scanning system.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We amassed in total 15 mocap datasets... The publicly available datasets were downloaded from the internet. We obtained several other datasets privately or recorded them ourselves

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: Due to inherent problems with mocap, such as swapped and mislabeled markers, we manually inspected the results and either corrected or held out problems.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets... Each dataset was recorded using a different number of markers placed at different locations on the body... The input is sparse markers... high resolution 4D scanning system.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: We achieve this using a new method, MoSh++, that converts mocap data into realistic 3D human meshes represented by a rigged body model

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: The vertex positions of SMPL are adapted according to identity-dependent shape parameters... AMASS has 42 hours of mocap, 346 subjects, and 11451 motions.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The consistent representation of AMASS makes it readily useful for animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep leaming.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: We make AMASS available to the research community at http://amass.is.tue.mpg.de , and will support the community in adding new captures as long as they can be similarly shared.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: The source datasets all contain varying markersets ranging in size from 37 to 91 markers; AMASS unifies these into a single format. Each frame in AMASS includes the SMPL 3D shape parameters ( 16dimensions), the DMPL soft tissue coefficients ( 8dimensions), and the full SMPL pose parameters ( 90dimensions), including hand articulations.
